meta.move: Strong path: owns the missed call, then evidence in order, then the rewrite
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have twenty minutes before a client call, so let's start with who decided to put a zero on Owen's essay, and whether anyone spoke to him first.
Ms. Kalinowski, thank you for coming in. Before anything else: I entered that zero before I called you, and that was wrong. I'm sorry.
Okay. Owen found out from the gradebook, on his phone, in the middle of class. Procedure 4.2 says a parent is contacted before any mark is entered, so what was the zero based on?

Here's what I can show you. The document's version history: created at 11:31 PM the night before it was due, title only. At 11:52, 612 words arrive in one edit. At 11:58, another 794. No drafts before that.
I'm writing down 11:31, 11:52 and 11:58. Procedure 4.1 says you speak with the student first, and nobody called me, so did you speak to Owen before you entered the zero?
Second, the essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' That line is not in Hamlet. Here's the scene; you can search it yourself.
I'm writing that down, and I'll search it myself. A misquoted line is a student misremembering a play, Hale, and I've seen worse in sworn statements. What else do you have?

Our procedure allows a supervised rewrite for a first concern. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. We could do it in my room, Thursday at 8:15, with the vice-principal supervising.
That's 4.4. I'll want it in writing tonight: private, not in front of his class, and nothing on his record. Until then, the zero comes off the gradebook.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You offered Owen a supervised rewrite on Thursday at 8:15 in your room with the vice-principal, its mark to replace the zero with nothing placed on his record. I still require that offer confirmed in writing, kept private and away from his class, and the zero removed from the gradebook until then. I expect it in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: fallback, not the last position: she accepted that 4.4 meets her demand about his record but has not agreed to the rewrite, and she still wants it in writing, private, with the zero off the gradebook; that is close to the fair outcome, a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record, but nothing is confirmed yet, and her time did not run out.
What moved her: you let her search the misquoted line in the play herself, because it was specific, tied to his essay and something she could check on her own.
What cost ground: you never answered her question about whether you spoke with Owen before entering the zero, so her complaint about procedure stayed open.
What she never said: in October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history with its late-night times the evening before the due date came very close to that night, which proves nothing about the essay, and it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: when she asks whether you spoke with Owen first, answer it directly before you move on to your documents.
